study_identification_part.si4_title: Nomograms of human hippocampal volume shifted by polygenic scores

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate whether incorporating hippocampal-volume polygenic scores (HV-PGS) into normative nomograms of hippocampal volume improves clinical utility, by building GPR-based nomograms in UK Biobank and assessing impact and clinical application in ADNI.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states that 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 from the UK Biobank (UKB) were used to build HV nomograms. The application number is also provided (65299).
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Using imaging data from 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 from the UK Biobank (UKB), we built HV nomograms using Gaussian process regression (GPR)... Data from a total of 39,664 subjects (18,718 female) aged 44-82 were obtained from the UKB (application number 65299) with available genotyping and imaging data.
rci1_dataset_name.location: Janahi2022.pdf.md: Abstract (line 41); Materials and methods / Datasets (lines 216-217)

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Genetically adjusted GPR nomograms shift by ~100 mm^3 (~2.3% of average HV; ~3 years of aging at ~65) and reduce intra-diagnostic variance by ~68% in ADNI, though survival analysis for MCI-to-AD conversion shows no significant improvement.
